items.title: The uv installer does not respect HTTPS_PROXY on Windows
items.reason: The same Windows self-update archive-download stage failed while version checks and other uv downloads worked. Maintainer discussion identified the PowerShell installer. Its HTTP proxy configuration/authentication problem was fixed through axodotdev/cargo-dist#2078; the new report instead rejects the SOCKS5 scheme after reading ALL_PROXY.

items.title: Powershell installer: respect HTTPS_PROXY and ANY_PROXY env vars
items.reason: The upstream fix linked from astral-sh/uv#10709 added explicit proxy environment handling to the PowerShell installer. Despite ANY_PROXY in its title, the implementation reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY and constructs System.Net.WebProxy for WebClient. It did not introduce a SOCKS-capable downloader.

items.title: standalone installer for Windows - NO_PROXY environment variable is not applied
items.reason: Another current defect in the same generated PowerShell proxy helper. It concerns bypassing proxies for internal hosts, not connecting through SOCKS5. Its upstream issue axodotdev/cargo-dist#2538 and open fix axodotdev/cargo-dist#2539 only address NO_PROXY, so they do not centralize this report.

items.title: Support for SOCKS5 and SOCKS5H
items.reason: The historical SOCKS support request was closed with astral-sh/uv#7503. It concerns uv's reqwest client, whereas this report fails inside the separate PowerShell installer; it is not evidence that Windows self-update previously supported SOCKS5.

items.title: Add `socks` support
items.reason: Merged on 2024-09-18, this enabled reqwest's socks feature and added its dependency. The diff does not change the PowerShell installer. It supports the distinction between successful uvx downloads and failing self-update archive downloads, rather than establishing a regression.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues using ServicePointManager, "does not support proxies", SOCKS5, SOCKS5H, socks, ALL_PROXY, "self update" with proxy/SOCKS5/reqwest, installer proxy, PowerShell proxy, WebClient, and area:windows proxy searches, including searches without versions or platforms. Searched open, closed, and merged pull requests for proxy, socks/SOCKS5, self update, and cargo-dist. PR searches returned no matches even for known linked history, so inspected referenced PRs directly, including astral-sh/uv#7503 and astral-sh/uv#15798, and followed upstream discussions and fixes. Inspected candidate comments and the astral-sh/uv#22265 cross-reference chain to axodotdev/cargo-dist#2538 and axodotdev/cargo-dist#2539. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#10709 as the same bug because it addressed HTTP proxy configuration/authentication; astral-sh/uv#22265 addresses NO_PROXY. Also ruled out astral-sh/uv#15970 (mirror configuration), astral-sh/uv#10724 (certificate trust), and astral-sh/uv#16309 (generic WebClient exception without a confirmed SOCKS mechanism). Checked current uv source and the pinned cargo-dist v0.32.0 PowerShell template. No existing item found tracks this exact SOCKS5 archive-download failure.

type_reason: Windows self-update fails to download an available update through SOCKS5 even though uv's Rust HTTP client supports that proxy scheme. The source confirms a separate PowerShell archive-download path using WebClient/WebProxy, consistent with the reported ServicePointManager error. The closest historical fixes enabled Rust-client SOCKS support or installer HTTP proxy configuration; neither establishes prior SOCKS support in this installer path. No same-problem duplicate or previously fixed regression was established.
summary: A separate Windows installer bug. astral-sh/uv#10709 and axodotdev/cargo-dist#2078 cover historical HTTP proxy handling; astral-sh/uv#22265 covers NO_PROXY. astral-sh/uv#4227 and astral-sh/uv#7503 added SOCKS support to uv's Rust client, not the PowerShell archive downloader.
draft_response:
uv's Rust HTTP client supports SOCKS5 through astral-sh/uv#7503, but Windows self-update runs a separate PowerShell installer whose archive download uses WebClient/WebProxy. Your ServicePointManager error comes from that download stage. The HTTP proxy fix associated with astral-sh/uv#10709 did not add SOCKS support there.

This needs a SOCKS-capable download path in the cargo-dist PowerShell installer. If your proxy also provides an HTTP endpoint, try setting HTTPS_PROXY to that endpoint before updating; the installer prioritizes it over ALL_PROXY.
